sources.why: Cloudflare's own skills for the developer platform. Curated across every agent that already had them — see docs/adr/0003. The repo also ships commands/ and rules/, which only its Claude Code plugin installs; skipped deliberately.

skills.name: cloudflare
skills.why: Umbrella platform skill — Workers, storage, AI, networking, security. Retrieval-first over live Cloudflare docs rather than pre-trained knowledge.

skills.name: wrangler
skills.why: Correct CLI syntax for deploys and resource management. Worth having loaded before any wrangler command.

skills.name: workers-best-practices
skills.why: Catches the Workers anti-patterns that bite in production — floating promises, global state, streaming, secrets.

skills.name: durable-objects
skills.why: Stateful coordination: RPC methods, SQLite storage, alarms, WebSockets, and the wrangler config to match.

skills.name: agents-sdk
skills.why: Building agents on Workers — durable execution, queues, retries, React hooks.

skills.name: sandbox-stable
skills.why: Sandboxed execution of untrusted or generated code on the stable @cloudflare/sandbox package. Replaces the old sandbox-sdk skill, which upstream split into sandbox-stable / sandbox-next / sandbox-migrate-to-next; the other two only matter on the 1.0 preview.

skills.name: cloudflare-email-service
skills.why: Transactional email end to end, including the SPF/DKIM/DMARC config that's easy to get wrong.

skills.name: turnstile-spin
skills.why: Wires Turnstile through the whole stack, including canonical server-side siteverify.

skills.name: web-perf
skills.why: Core Web Vitals and load analysis via Chrome DevTools MCP.

skills.name: cloudflare-one
skills.why: Zero Trust and SASE — Access, Gateway, WARP, Tunnel, device posture.

skills.name: cloudflare-one-migrations
skills.why: Migration planning off Zscaler, Palo Alto, or a legacy VPN. Paired with cloudflare-one.

sources.why: The repo this one forked from. These are the skills worth tracking upstream rather than owning — see docs/adr/0001.

skills.name: code-review
skills.why: Reviews changes since a fixed point on two axes — repo standards and the originating spec.

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.why: Deep-module vocabulary. Shared dependency of grilling and improve-codebase-architecture.

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.why: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions.

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.why: Maintains ubiquitous language and ADRs. Shared dependency of grill-with-docs.

skills.name: grill-me
skills.why: User-invoked entry point to the grilling interview.

skills.name: grill-with-docs
skills.why: Grilling that writes ADRs and a glossary as it goes. Needs domain-modeling.

skills.name: grilling
skills.why: The interview engine itself. Required by grill-me and grill-with-docs.

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skills.why: Scans for deepening opportunities and grills through the one you pick. Needs codebase-design.

skills.name: prototype
skills.why: Throwaway prototypes to sanity-check a state model or UI before committing to it.

skills.name: research
skills.why: Delegates reading legwork to a background agent and lands findings as Markdown in the repo.

sources.why: Cursor's plugin monorepo — 78 skills across many kits. Exactly one is curated.

skills.name: thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review
skills.why: User-invoked, deliberately harsh maintainability review of a branch: abstraction quality, giant files, spaghetti conditions, and restructurings that make the code simpler without changing behaviour. Sits alongside code-review rather than replacing it — that one checks standards and spec, this one attacks the structure. Upstream also ships thermo-nuclear-review (security/correctness) and thermos (runs both); neither is curated, so don't reach for thermos.

sources.why: Vercel's public skill collection; only the discovery skill is curated from it.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.why: Finds and installs skills on demand — the discovery front-end to everything else.
